forecast-period.text: A low pressure system centred over southeastern NSW will continue to move eastwards and a high pressure system in the Bight to slowly drift eastwards. The high weakens today allowing a cold front to move over the south of the state on Wednesday. Another ridge of high pressure follows on Thursday, with another cold front clipping the southeast on Friday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible morning fog patches about central and western districts. Maximum temperatures near to below average grading to above average in the west. Southwest to southeasterly winds tending northeast to northerly in the west.

Showers extending across the agricultural areas, with possible thunderstorms about eastern parts. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast grading to below average about the agricultural areas. Light winds tending northwesterly ahead of a fresh and gusty southwest to southerly change extending throughout the day.
Possible light morning showers about windward coast and ranges. Maximum temperatures generally below average. Generally southwest to southeasterly winds.

text.p: Showers about windward coasts, extending across the southern agricultural area from late morning. Maximum temperatures below average about the southern agricultural area, grading to above average in the north and west. Light winds, shifting north to northwesterly ahead of a fresh southwest to southeasterly change extending throughout during the afternoon and evening.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: less than 2 mm about the northern agricultural area, south of the pastoral districts and about the northeast, increasing to 2 to 10 mm across the southern agricultural area, with possible falls of 10 to 20 mm about the Lower South East district and with thunderstorms.
